subject: Stabilizer / true-up amendment for Order Form - Orinoco Health
messages:
From: Danielle Rivera <d.rivera@orinocohealth.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com
Cc: finance@orinocohealth.com
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Orinoco - suggested edits to pricing stabilizer / true-up

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the productive call yesterday. Our GC flagged the pricing section in the order form — specifically the 'True-up and Floor/Cap' paragraph in Exhibit A. They're concerned the current formulation (step-up floor + immediate true-up payment on quarterly invoices) creates a sharp billing cliff for us if usage spikes during initial ramp.

Attached is our marked-up copy with two asks:
- Replace the current "immediate quarterly true-up" language with a "3-month trailing average true-up" to smooth billing impact.
- Add a temporary startup stabilizer (6 months) that caps the quarterly invoice increase to +25% vs prior quarter if growth > 40%.

Can Redwood accept a temporary collar and trailing average mechanism? If not, please propose alternative guardrails. We want to avoid a big unexpected invoice with final acceptance.

Attachment: Orinoco_orderform_marked.pdf (PDF, 83KB)

Best,
Danielle Rivera
Head of Procurement
Orinoco Health
[d.rivera@orinocohealth.com]

From: lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com
To: Danielle Rivera <d.rivera@orinocohealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com, grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Orinoco - suggested edits to pricing stabilizer / true-up

Danielle — thanks for the clear note and the marked-up PDF; appreciate the detail. Looping in Rishi (pricing & contracts) and Grace (AE) to propose an acceptable middle ground.

Initial thoughts: we want to preserve predictability on minimum commitments and the ability to true-up to the committed band, but we are open to a smoothing mechanism that protects you during early ramping months. Proposed approach from Redwood:

1) 3-month trailing average for true-up basis (agrees with your ask).
2) Startup stabilizer: first two full billing quarters after go-live, quarterly increases capping at +30% (we can consider 25% if you can take slightly higher minimum commit term).
3) Coupon / discount trade: in exchange for a lower cap (25% v 30%), Redwood would offer a one-time implementation credit applied to Q2 invoice.

Rishi — can you draft concise language for Exhibit A that implements the trailing-average calculation and the temporary cap? Grace — is this acceptable commercially so we can get DocuSign ready?

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
[lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com]

Attachment: RDW-counter-20270225.pdf (Redline PDF, 47KB)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com, Danielle Rivera <d.rivera@orinocohealth.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 23 Feb 2027 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Orinoco - suggested edits to pricing stabilizer / true-up

Hi all — draft language below (proposed Exhibit A insert). I've kept it deliberately prescriptive to reduce back-and-forth with legal: 

"True-up and Stabilizer. For the purposes of invoice true-up, actual usage for any quarter will be calculated as the three-calendar-month trailing average of monthly billable units. Upon true-up, any increase to the invoice relative to the immediately preceding quarterly invoice shall be subject to a Startup Stabilizer for the first two full billing quarters following go-live, which will cap invoice increases at 30% (thirty percent) over the prior quarter. After the Stabilizer period, standard true-up and minimum-commitment remediation applies. In the event Customer growth causes invoice increases that exceed the Stabilizer cap, Redwood will work with Customer to establish a one-time phased true-up payment plan over up to two additional billing cycles at Customer request."

Notes: 
- I left it at 30% to preserve some protection for Redwood on abrupt usage surges. If Orinoco confirms they can accept a slightly higher minimum commitment term (9 v 6 months), we can reduce the cap to 25% and offer a $25k implementation credit as Lauren suggested.
- If you want the formula spelled out for per-unit pricing (e.g., embeddings per 1k tokens), I can append the calculation table; I included a CSV 'pricing-matrix-3mo-trailing.csv' for clarity.

Attachment: pricing-matrix-3mo-trailing.csv (CSV, 4KB)

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Pricing & Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Danielle Rivera <d.rivera@orinocohealth.com>

Date: Wed, 24 Feb 2027 11:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Orinoco - suggested edits to pricing stabilizer / true-up

Thanks Rishi — that reads much cleaner. Two requests from legal/finance after reviewing your draft: 
1) Replace the phrase "phased true-up payment plan" with a distinct optional mechanism: "deferred true-up spread over two equal installments due with the next two quarterly invoices" — they prefer fixed installments for audit clarity.
2) Add a carve-out: if usage is driven by an M&A event or change of control (customer consolidation of services), the Stabilizer does not apply and immediate true-up to committed bands may be enforced.

If you can accept those two small belt-and-suspenders edits, we can route to procurement and sign.

Attachment: (no change to Orinoco marked PDF)

--
Danielle Rivera

Orinoco Health

From: rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com
To: Danielle Rivera <d.rivera@orinocohealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com, grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 26 Feb 2027 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Orinoco - suggested edits to pricing stabilizer / true-up

Danielle — we can do both edits with minor tweaks. Proposed final paragraph insertion: 

"Deferred True-up Installments. If Customer growth during the Stabilizer period would otherwise result in a true-up amount exceeding the Stabilizer cap, Customer may elect to defer the excess amount, which will be amortized over two equal installments and invoiced with the next two quarterly invoices following election. Such election must be made in writing within 30 days of the true-up notice.

Carve-out. The Stabilizer shall not apply to usage attributable to (a) a change in control of Customer, or (b) a material acquisition or consolidation event of Customer’s business lines that materially increases demand for the Services; in such events Redwood may apply immediate true-up to committed bands."

We will lower the Stabilizer cap to 25% if Orinoco agrees to an extended 9-month minimum commit and the $25k implementation credit noted earlier. If you prefer, we can set the DocuSign with the 30% / 6-month config and include an amendment path to move to 25% / 9-month with the credit at a later date.

Grace — commercial sign-off?

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Pricing & Contracts
Redwood Inference

- Option B (Preferred): 25% Stabilizer cap, 9-month Stabilizer window, $25,000 implementation credit applied Q2.

Please confirm which option you prefer and we’ll prepare the final Exhibit A text and DocuSign package. If you want the lower cap now but need procurement to approve the 9-month term, we can include language to convert automatically upon purchase order execution.
